facts.text: A point cloud is a large set of measured points in three-dimensional space, each with an x, y and z position and often a brightness value, that together outline the shapes around a sensor.
facts.quote: A point cloud is a large set of measured points in three-dimensional space, each with an x, y and z position and often a brightness value, that together outline the shapes around a sensor.

facts.text: A lidar on a machine produces tens of thousands of points ten or more times per second, each with position, intensity, return number and time stamp.
facts.quote: a lidar on a machine produces tens of thousands of points, ten or more times per second, each with position, intensity, return number and time stamp.

facts.text: Point clouds are the raw data used by lidar and some radars and depth cameras; perception groups the points into objects and tracks those objects.
facts.quote: Point clouds are the raw language of lidar and some radars and depth cameras. Perception groups the points into objects and tracks them.

facts.text: A real site can be converted into a virtual site using lidar plus an inertial unit or satellite positioning to obtain a directly mapped point cloud, which is cleaned and turned into terrain and objects.
facts.quote: lidar plus an inertial unit or satellite positioning gives a directly mapped cloud, which is then cleaned and turned into terrain and objects [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Simulated and real point clouds are compared using distribution measures because individual points are partly random and two scans of the same scene never match point for point.
facts.quote: Because individual points are partly random, two scans of the same scene never match point for point, so simulated and real clouds are compared with distribution measures.

facts.text: The booklet lists Chamfer distance among measures for comparing simulated and real point clouds and reports that density-aware Chamfer distance (DCD) correlated best with perception results in a November 2025 study.
facts.quote: The booklet lists Chamfer distance and others, and reports a November 2025 study in which the density-aware Chamfer distance (DCD) correlated best with perception results

facts.text: In the November 2025 point-cloud study reported by the booklet, real and simulated scans averaged a density-aware Chamfer distance (DCD) of 0.63 with only 21% segmentation agreement.
facts.quote: real and simulated scans averaged a DCD of 0.63 with only 21% segmentation agreement [Chapter 6].

facts.text: One radar simulation produced about 12% of the real point density—251 versus 2,057 points per frame—because the model lacked diffuse scattering and multiple bounces present in real radar.
facts.quote: one radar simulation produced about 12% of the real density (251 against 2,057 points per frame) because real radar includes diffuse scattering and multiple bounces the model lacked [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Dust, rain and snow add false points in the air to point clouds and remove points from real surfaces.
facts.quote: Dust, rain and snow add false points in the air and remove points from real surfaces

facts.text: Off-road point-cloud de-dusting filters scored 97.55% on their own data.
facts.quote: off-road "de-dusting" filters scored 97.55% on their own data

facts.text: A construction fusion model fell to 65.58% in one dense-dust case, compared with 94.85% to 96.73% elsewhere.
facts.quote: a construction fusion model fell to 65.58% in one dense-dust case against 94.85% to 96.73% elsewhere [Chapter 13].

facts.text: The booklet recommends recording point clouds in the rawest useful form with timestamps, positions, return and intensity, rather than recording a thinned visualization cloud.
facts.quote: For recordings, the booklet asks for the rawest useful form, timestamps, positions, return and intensity, rather than a thinned visualization cloud [Chapter 5].

facts.text: Point-cloud realism is central to the sensor-model credibility argument because point clouds are both what lidar perception consumes and what a lidar simulator must reproduce.
facts.quote: A point cloud is both what lidar perception consumes and what a lidar simulator must reproduce, so "is this simulated cloud realistic enough" sits at the heart of the sensor-model credibility argument

facts.text: The booklet finds no single accepted realism score for point clouds.
facts.quote: the booklet finds no single accepted realism score [Chapter 6].
